newsitem.title: UK: Med gasoline weaker, naphtha balanced.
newsitem.headline: Med gasoline weaker, naphtha balanced.

text.p: Med oil products were mixed on Wednesday with gasoline weaker, naphtha balanced and fuel oil balanced to weakish, traders said.
Gasoline was notionally weaker, under the influence of falling prices on futures markets.

Dealers said the region remains bare of high octane material in the prompt period. "I do not think there will be much of that around until mid June, one refiner in Italy said. Low octane material was in better supply.
A refiner earlier heard to be seeking 10,000 tonnes of Eurograde gasoline covered the requirement from within the company's own system.
Naphtha was relatively balanced. Supplies of Algerian and Greek material were on show, one end user in the Med said.
Gas oil was a mixed bag. Traders said they expected outright prices to edge lower as sharp drops in benchmark IPE futures pressured prices lower.
EN590 continued to be fairly buoyant with short supply making for fairly elevated premiums.
Traders assessed premiums at around quotes fob hi +$3.0/+$5.0 cif NWE.

Few thought this situation would continue. "I don't think so many Mediterranean cargoes will head out of the region in July and it only takes one or two cargoes to change the balance," said one trader.
High sulphur cargoes were said to be balanced to slightly weakish after a cargo reported sold by a trader to a refiner at high cif plus $3 on Tuesday.
A few cargoes are yet to find buyers, weighing on the market, traders said.
Traders said that Egypt on Tuesday closed its tender for the sale of one percent material out of Alexandria and the results should be out by June 23.
